answers.answer: Layoffs are triggered when it is necessary to decrease the number of teachers. Teachers are laid off in the inverse order of their seniority within their classification (least seniority first); if seniority is equal, a lottery determines the layoff. Teachers must be notified in writing. Seniority is based on length of actual service in the classification with NH State Department certification (Elementary, Secondary by subject, Special subject by specialty, Middle school by subject/grade). Displaced teachers may add years in a previous classification to their new classification's seniority. Seniority lists are established by the Administration by February 1 of each year for employees who are not on a continuing contract and revised every twelve (12) months, transmitted to the Association, and remain unchanged during military and maternity leave. Laid-off teachers are recalled in reverse order (highest seniority first) via registered/certified mail. Teachers must respond to the Superintendent within ten (10) calendar days of receiving the recall notice. Laid-off teachers remain on the recall list for 24 months unless they waive rights, resign, fail to accept recall, or fail to report within 30 days. Seniority is broken by discharge, voluntary quit, failure to respond to a recall notice, or remaining on lay-off for more than 24 months. No new teachers may be hired while certified laid-off teachers are available to fill vacancies. If a laid-off teacher accepts a less-than-full-time position, they forfeit recall rights for the remainder of the academic year but remain on the recall list for the next school year. Laid-off teachers are given first refusal for substitute teaching opportunities ranked by seniority, provided they notify the Superintendent in writing prior to the first day for students. Any employee on lay-off shall not be prevented from securing employment during the lay-off period.
